newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French consumer prices fall in August.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French consumer prices fall in August.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on a fall of 0.2 to 0.3 percent in French consumer prices in August, reported by national statistics institute INSEE on Friday.
It's weaker than expected...it confirms there's no inflation in France and we now expect further easing on rates, at least the call-money rate. There's absolutely no inflationary tension.
PHILIPPE CHEVAL, ECONOMIST, BANQUE NATIONALE DE PARIS

It shows a clear slowdown in the rise in prices. It is partly due to the fact that the increase (last August) in Value Added Tax is no longer having an effect, but we thought this would be more gradual. It goes further than the effect of the tax changes. There is a slowdown in underlying inflation.
Excluding public tariffs and corrected for the impact of the tax measures, inflation is about one percent. If you want to talk about deflation this figure would have to be negative.
That does not mean that prices in some sectors, notably in industry, are not falling.
JEAN LOUIS MOURIER, ECONOMIST, LOUIS DREYFUS FINANCE.
It's a bigger fall than expected, we're seeing the effects of the VAT increase disappearing. Now inflation has fallen three straight months in a row. It's a little worrying.

We were expecting a 0.1 fall month-on-month. Two things -- the fall in the year-on-year rate reflects the entering in the base of last year's VAT hike. Having said that, clearly the monthly decline is bigger than expected.

Essentially, this is due to the volatile component of food products. Fresh products were down 10 percent. But, at same time, there's continuation of the trend in private sector manufactured products, which fell 0.1 percent when you exclude clothing.

It's not a very positive sign for the economy as it highlights sluggish demand. I don't buy this deflation theory. What we're seeing are essentialy seasonal declines in CPI. Having said that, it's also clear there are very few inflationary pressures because of a weak economy. It's a question of level and magnitude. We're not in a deflation environment but we are in a weak economy.
We had three months of falling prices in a period when prices are always subdued. I'd need to see it in a period when prices do not usually fall.
